what_it_does: Designing a many-core processor chip for wireless baseband (the part of a radio that encodes and decodes signals) normally requires running a detailed chip blueprint simulation, which is so slow it takes days or weeks. This paper builds a fast simulation framework that translates the chip's software instructions into a form that runs directly on a regular computer, paired with a rough-but-fast timing model of a 1,024-core RISC-V (a popular open processor design) chip. The simulator also connects to realistic wireless channel models so engineers can test 5G signal-processing algorithms end to end. Running on a single CPU core it is roughly 1,000 times faster than blueprint-level simulation; using 128 parallel CPU threads it speeds up by another 73–121 times. Be appropriately hedged — the exact accuracy trade-offs between the timing approximation and a real chip are not characterized in the abstract.
